gaps.gap: Complaint hand-over: the trigger and the human are sourced (CPR 2.1.7, 26.7.2, licence 9.1) and the complaint has clocks (acknowledge at once by telephone, 26.13.3; conclude in twenty business days, 26.14.2); the transfer has none: what the agent does when the conversation turns, when the human is in it, whether the time is recorded. QoS T1(2a) measures only the wait after the IVR choice.

searched.quote: preclude the use of non-human agents by Licensees in conversations with Consumers regarding Consumer Complaints.

searched.says: A duty to help a Consumer formulate and lodge a complaint; no step for an automated channel.
searched.quote: reasonably assist any Consumer, so requesting such assistance, to formulate and to lodge a Consumer Complaint with the Licensee

searched.says: Complaints resolved properly and promptly; no step for the moment an automated conversation turns into one.
searched.quote: investigate and resolve Consumer Complaints properly and promptly

searched.says: Trained people respond in a timely and prompt manner; no time stated.
searched.quote: receive, process, and respond to Consumer Complaints in a timely and prompt manner

searched.says: Acknowledgement with a reference number and an indicative time-frame; nothing on who or what issues it on an automated channel.
searched.quote: acknowledge the receipt of each Consumer Complaint by providing the complainant with a reference number for the complaint and the indicative time-frame

searched.says: The acknowledgement clock: at once by telephone or visit, one business day for a written complaint. Chat and app are not named; an acknowledgement is not a hand-over.
searched.quote: immediately in the case of complaints submitted by telephone or personal visit, and within one (1) business day in the case of a written complaint

searched.says: Resolve on first contact where possible; with 26.7.2 the first contact on an automated channel cannot be the one that resolves.
searched.quote: Where possible, Licensees shall seek to resolve a Consumer Complaint on first contact.

searched.says: The conclusion clock: twenty business days. A clock for the complaint, not for the transfer to a person.
searched.quote: conclude Consumer Complaints within twenty (20) business days after receipt or as soon as practical in all circumstances

searched.says: Trained personnel for complaints, at licence level, on every channel (Arabic: موظفين مدربين). No hand-over procedure or time.
searched.quote: The Licensee shall maintain adequate trained personnel to receive and respond promptly to complaints and disputes from Customers.

searched.says: Annex A, T1(2a): the only time measured is the wait after the IVR choice, under two minutes, indicative. A bot before that choice, and chat or app, are unmeasured.
searched.quote: Average time (seconds) spent waiting from the time the Customer has selected the IVR choice to speak to an agent until the Customer is connected to an agent

searched.says: Trade Law 14/2023: complaint numbers and means always available with qualified staff; a staffed complaint channel, no stop, hand-over or clock for an AI chat.
searched.quote: Designate numbers and means of communication regarding complaints, which shall be always available without interruption with qualified staff

gaps.uae_position: The human requirement is binding (26.7.2, licence 9.1) and Mizan enforces it. The CPR wants first-contact resolution (26.14.1) and bars the machine from the conversation (26.7.2); nothing joins the two: no text says what an automated channel must do at the moment a conversation becomes a complaint, or how fast the human must take over. The acknowledgement clock (26.13.3) names telephone, visit and written complaints, not chat or app, and a reference number is not a conversation.

gaps.gap: Consent elicited by an AI: the CPR accepts spoken consent if it can be stored (4.7.2) and decides by sales medium (4.10, 4.17, 4.22) whether an OTP is needed, naming no AI channel; the PDPL permits the processing the contract needs without consent (4(9)) and wants any further processing consented 'in writing or electronically' (6(1)(b)); one spoken 'yes' buys the service and consents to nothing beyond it, and nobody has said which medium an AI chat or voice agent is.

searched.quote: all tangible forms of consent: written; spoken; and, electronic interaction are acceptable

searched.says: Digital applications: multi-step, 2FA unless expressly specified otherwise.
searched.quote: unless objectively justified otherwise, or expressly specified otherwise, the process shall require the consumer to complete a 2FA procedure

searched.says: Where 2FA is mandated, the default is an OTP.
searched.quote: the default method of 2FA shall, in the absence of any approved alternative, be one-time password (OTP).

searched.says: Call-centre purchases: recorded verbal consent, no 2FA. A voice agent reads naturally as this.
searched.quote: where a Service is purchased via a telephone call to/from a Licensee

searched.says: Licensee App purchases: no express 2FA. A chat agent in the app reads as this or as 4.10.
searched.quote: where the purchase of a Licensee provided Service3 is made via a Licensee App

searched.says: What an automated system sends is the operator's own act.
searched.quote: If it is sent by an electronic medium automated and programmed to operate automatically by or on behalf of the Originator.

searched.says: Processing the contract needs is permitted without consent; the seam is only for processing beyond it.
searched.quote: If the processing is necessary to perform a contract to which the Data Subject is a party, or to take measures at the request of the Data Subject with the aim of concluding, amending or terminating a contract.

searched.says: Data-processing consent in writing or electronically; spoken is not named.
searched.quote: whether in writing or electronically

searched.says: Trade Law 14/2023: a digital contract is valid on offer and acceptance that meet the digital identity and digital signature requirements; no medium is named for spoken consent through an AI channel.
searched.quote: Fulfillment of the offer and acceptance and the contractual relationship executed upon satisfying the requirements of the digital identity and digital signature.

gaps.uae_position: No CPR sales medium names a conversational agent, so whether an AI-elicited purchase needs an OTP depends on a classification no text makes. The processing the contract needs is lawful without consent (4(9)); a spoken consent through the agent covers the purchase (4.7.2) but not a processing purpose beyond the contract, which 6(1)(b) wants in writing or electronically. Mizan takes the strict reading (4.10 plus OTP, 4.11).

gaps.line: No metric for where an agent's authority ends
gaps.gap: Standards gap, addressed to ITU. Mapped first: Mizan's stop at S2-3 sits at Y.3173 'Human and System' on the decision step (7.2, Table 7-1, p. 6: "a) Human; b) Human and System; c) System."), and its hand-over is Readiness 2.0 D9's inference-to-action latency in the other direction (p. 27: "inference-to-action latency: average time from first inference to human action"; there the AI alerts and the human acts). Readiness 2.0 also measures the human shaping the inference (D8, p. 25) and states that accountability of final decisions remains with humans (D10, p. 29). Mapped there, neither text measures when an acting agent must stop, how often it hands over or how long that takes: the stop point, the hand-over rate, the hand-over latency. Y.3173 Table 7-2 NOTE 1 (p. 7) gives a human's order the highest authority ("decisions and execution instructions provided by a human being have the highest authority"); it never requires the system to ask. Y.3173 cites SAE J3016 and drops its fallback column, the request to intervene (Appendix I.1, Table I.1, p. 12 to 13).
